title: BCDR Essentials: Build Resilient Continuity Plans
summary: Build a BCDR plan that holds up under pressure: BIA, RTO/RPO targets, ransomware-resistant backups, compliance overlap, and common failure modes.
body_text: A ransomware infection takes a manufacturing client’s primary file servers and shared drives offline mid-shift. Production stops, orders queue up, and the next 72 hours determine whether the business absorbs the disruption or hands clients to a competitor. Business continuity disaster recovery (BCDR) combines two disciplines: keeping operations running during a disruption and recovering IT systems afterward. For MSPs and IT directors with lean teams, BCDR planning separates a manageable incident from a business crisis. This article covers BCDR plan components, implementation and testing, deployment models, ransomware recovery, compliance, and common failure points. Why business continuity disaster recovery plans matter BCDR plans matter because documented recovery priorities and decision paths determine whether an outage stays contained or becomes a business crisis. Many MSPs protecting small to medium sized businesses operate without a documented plan, and that gap between confidence and reality is where the risk lives. The financial weight is real: the global average breach cost hit $4.44 million ( IBM 2025 ), with operational disruption still driving the bulk of the cost. Here’s why that matters: a single unrecoverable outage cascades across customer relationships, audit standing, and revenue, regardless of whether you manage one environment for an enterprise or two hundred for clients. How business continuity and disaster recovery work together Business continuity and disaster recovery cover two sides of the same disruption. Business continuity (BC) governs operations during the event: communication plans, manual workarounds, and staffing decisions. Disaster recovery (DR) focuses on recovering IT systems, data, and infrastructure in a defined sequence. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) places the Business Continuity Plan (BCP) at the organization, business, or mission level and the Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) at the system level, with the DRP focused on recovering IT systems after a disaster. The Business Impact Analysis (BIA) connects both layers by identifying critical processes, mapping them to IT systems, and establishing acceptable downtime and data loss thresholds. What a BCDR plan includes A defensible BCDR plan includes a BIA, recovery targets, backup and redundancy strategy, and clearly assigned roles. Here’s the thing: those components of a defensible BCDR plan feed into each other, and skipping one creates gaps that surface during a real incident. Business Impact Analysis drives every recovery decision The BIA is foundational. NIST and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) treat BIA as an early planning step , while the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency ( CISA ) places it early in planning materials. A risk assessment documents potential threats, their likelihood, and impact on systems identified in the BIA, producing a prioritized threat list and risk treatment plan. Without a completed BIA and risk assessment, teams lack a defensible basis for prioritizing either the BCP or the DRP. RTO and RPO set the recovery boundaries Recovery Time Objective ( RTO ) defines how long a system can be unavailable before the impact becomes unacceptable. Recovery Point Objective (RPO) defines how much data loss is tolerable, measured backward from the moment of disruption. What this looks like in practice: teams set both per system, not as a single organization-wide number. RTO measures time availability; RPO measures data recoverability. Treating them as equivalent creates planning gaps. Backup, redundancy, and defined roles complete the plan Backup strategy follows directly from RPO targets: a one-hour RPO needs at least hourly backups or continuous replication. The 3-2-1 principle, three copies, two media types, one offsite, remains foundational, with the 3-2-1-1-0 evolution adding one immutable copy and zero unverified backup errors for ransomware environments. Document roles by position, not by name. Smaller organizations can combine roles but still need to assign each responsibility to a position. Store the plan outside any system an incident could compromise. How to implement and test a BCDR plan A BCDR plan works as a recurring cycle, not a one-time project. The play here is to treat implementation as an operating discipline. NIST SP 800-34 outlines a seven-phase process: establish policy, conduct the BIA, identify preventive controls, create recovery strategies, document the plan, test it, and maintain it. Testing exposes weaknesses. Tabletop exercises validate roles and decision-making, and CISA provides free templates with pre-built scenarios and after-action report formats. Failover testing goes further: disconnecting a critical system to confirm recovery architecture works under real conditions. Both are necessary, and the plan needs updating after every test, every incident, and every material infrastructure change. BCDR deployment models BCDR deployment models differ by recovery speed, management burden, geographic resilience, and cost. Architecture usually lands on the model matching downtime tolerance, data-loss tolerance, budget, and complexity. On-premises recovery keeps data local but concentrates risk On-premises DR uses owned hardware at a secondary location for local recovery speed and full data control, but it concentrates geographic risk and requires capital investment. Cloud-based recovery trades capex for geographic flexibility Cloud DR replicates to public cloud infrastructure, replacing secondary data center costs with geographic distribution. DRaaS offloads orchestration to a managed provider Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS) delivers pay-per-use recovery with contractually defined RTO and RPO. For teams building recurring revenue or lacking internal DR expertise, DRaaS removes the orchestration burden. Hybrid recovery layers local speed with cloud resilience Hybrid combines on-premises backup for rapid local recovery with cloud replication for site-level disasters. Mid-market organizations with mixed legacy and cloud workloads typically land here. How BCDR supports cyber resilience and ransomware recovery BCDR supports cyber resilience by making recovery possible even when attackers target production systems and backups together. Recovery architecture has to assume attackers will go after the backups first, and CISA documents that ransomware actors often delete or compromise system backups before triggering encryption. Bottom line: backup architecture must survive an adversary with network access. Immutable storage enforces write-once properties, preventing compromised credentials or ransomware processes from altering protected copies. Air-gapped storage, physical or logical, removes the persistent network path entirely. NIST CSF 2.0 requires verifying backup integrity before recovery (RC.RP-03) and confirming recovered asset integrity afterward (RC.RP-05). A recovery sequence that skips either step risks recovering into the same vulnerability. Compliance requirements that shape BCDR Compliance requirements turn BCDR into a documented obligation that has to satisfy auditors and operators at the same time. Three frameworks shape the conversation in most regulated environments: Healthcare organizations under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act ( HIPAA ) must maintain data backup, disaster recovery, and emergency mode operations plans. Continuity planning becomes part of day-to-day compliance, not just incident preparation. Any organization handling EU personal data faces General Data Protection Regulation ( GDPR ) Article 32, which mandates timely recovery of data availability with regular testing. That ties recoverability directly to both resilience and demonstrable process discipline. Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard ( PCI DSS ) v4.0 addresses incident response planning and coordination with related operational processes. In practice, BCDR cannot sit apart from the broader response workflow when payment environments are involved. Service Organization Control 2 ( SOC 2 ) covers BCDR through its Availability category and Common Criteria like CC7.5. The upshot: these frameworks overlap enough that one BCDR baseline can satisfy core requirements across them, with vertical-specific customization. For MSPs serving multiple regulated verticals, that shared baseline also acts as a service differentiator . Common reasons BCDR plans fail BCDR plans fail because priorities, dependencies, and recovery assumptions break down under real conditions. The most common pattern: backups exist, but end-to-end testing hasn’t occurred, so teams discover corrupted backups and unmapped dependencies during the actual incident. Teams skip RTO and RPO validation against real recovery conditions. Plans assume single-vector failures when incidents cascade across identity and endpoints simultaneously. Cloud workloads added since the last revision often sit outside the recovery sequence. How N‑able strengthens your BCDR Once planning, architecture, and validation are in place, execution under pressure determines the outcome. This means tooling matters because BCDR succeeds or fails in real environments. The N‑able platform follows a Before-During-After lifecycle across the full BCDR spectrum, covering resilience before an attack starts, during active response, and after systems need to recover. Before an attack, N‑able N‑central reduces the attack surface that triggers DR activation. N‑central handles unified endpoint management across Windows, macOS, and Linux, alongside automated patching, vulnerability prioritization, EDR, and DNS filtering. Self-healing workflows and a 700+ recipe automation library cut the manual work that creates configuration drift. During an attack, Adlumin MDR/XDR brings 24/7 detection and response across endpoints, identity, cloud, and network signals, paired with proprietary AI models that catch behaviors signature-based tools miss. Adlumin handles 90% automated remediation, meaning containment moves at machine speed while SOC analysts focus on cases that need human judgment. The platform analyzes 500 billion security events monthly across 11+ million endpoints. After an attack, Cove Data Protection shortens recovery windows through immutable-by-default cloud backup at 15-minute intervals. TrueDelta produces backups up to 60x smaller than image-based alternatives, automated recovery testing with AI/ML boot verification confirms recoverability before it is needed, and recovery options span file-level, full system-state, bare-metal, and dissimilar hardware restores. Where BCDR plans earn their value A BCDR plan has value only when it works under pressure. Organizations that recover quickly rehearse regularly, update after every change, and treat continuity as ongoing operational discipline. Whether you manage one environment or hundreds, know what matters most, know how fast you need it back, and prove the plan works before you need it. Contact us to see how N‑able supports BCDR across the full attack lifecycle. Data Resilience: Best Practices, from Attack Vectors to Remediation Attackers aren't stopping at production systems. They're targeting backups, too. Discover the best practices that can help protect your recovery strategy. Watch now Frequently Asked Questions About BCDR How often does a BCDR plan need to be tested? NIST guidance calls for contingency plans to be reviewed at least annually and revised after every incident and major system or environmental change. CISA emphasizes updating plans based on lessons learned and changes to the environment rather than prescribing a specific testing interval. What is the difference between RTO and RPO? RTO measures how long a system can stay offline before the business impact becomes unacceptable; RPO measures how much data loss is tolerable, counted backward from the moment of disruption. Both must be set per system based on BIA findings, not as blanket organization-wide numbers. Learn how each metric shapes your recovery strategy in our RTO vs. RPO guide . Do MSPs need their own BCDR plan separate from client plans? Yes. An MSP’s operational failure cascades across every client it serves, and CISA and NIST both address MSP risk explicitly as a vendor concern that clients increasingly audit. Can one BCDR plan satisfy multiple compliance frameworks? The core requirements for BIA, backup, disaster recovery, emergency operations, and testing appear across HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS, SOC 2, and NIST SP 800-34. A well-structured base plan can address all five with vertical-specific customization for regulated clients. What makes backups ransomware-resistant? Immutable storage prevents backups from being altered or deleted during a defined retention period, even by compromised administrator credentials. Air-gapped or logically isolated storage removes the persistent network path that ransomware uses to reach backup infrastructure. title: Moments: More Ways to Discover Your Next Favorite Game on Roblox
summary: Roblox launches new homepage with tabs for Moments, Chat, Me
body_text: Share News Product Moments: More Ways to Discover Your Next Favorite Game on Roblox Roblox’s App Now Offers Chat, Play, Discovery, and Creation in One Place By Seb Barrios, Senior Vice President of Engineering Published Jul 28, 2026 Today, players opening Roblox in Canada, New Zealand, and Singapore will begin to see a new app home, with tabs for Moments, Chat, and Me (those in New Zealand will also see Build ). Tabs will roll out globally* over the next several months. Moments is a new way to discover games: Players can watch gameplay clips from friends and video content creators, jumping into a fun game with one tap. Every Moment is a doorway to play. Chat lets players have one continuous conversation that travels seamlessly with them into a game—without leaving Roblox. Me brings avatar and profile into one place, making it easier for players to express themselves. Starting today, players in Canada, New Zealand, and Singapore will begin to see a new Roblox app with tabs for Moments, Chat, and Me. These tabs will roll out globally* over the coming months. For players in New Zealand, the new Build tab , an extension of Roblox Studio offering mobile-first creation in the app, will also begin to appear today. Every day, an average of 132 million active users come to Roblox looking to play one of millions of available games. And every day, our creator community releases even more games to try, from simulator and strategy games to high-fidelity, immersive multiplayer worlds. By matching players to the games they’ll truly enjoy and come back to again and again, we help creators build their business and find their most engaged audiences. Outside of Roblox, people may chat or share games in places where friends have to click three times and install an app to start playing. We want players to be able to recommend, discover, and find games all in one place without the extra steps. So we’re expanding the Roblox app to support the entire flow—one place to chat with friends, see what others are playing, and click directly into a great game. Earlier this year, we optimized our discovery and recommendation systems for games players stick with, surfacing relevant games on Roblox’s homepage via a player’s Recommended for You section. When Moments first launched as a beta, we envisioned it as an additional engine for game discovery. Today, Moments becomes a dedicated tab* on Roblox. With a diverse set of content from players and video content creators. Moments creates a frictionless way to see a game and play it with just one tap. Moments: Discover and Play New Games Instantly Moments is designed as a direct path from an exciting game to the people who will love it. Age-checked players 16 or older* can discover gameplay videos shared by friends and other players and try the game themselves with just one tap. Brand-new in the Moments tab are high-quality Roblox content videos by select content creators, similar to the content that players see these content creators sharing elsewhere. But in Moments, these videos not only share gameplay highlights, they link directly to the games they feature, so players can start playing with a single tap. As with our other discovery systems , Moments is optimized for players to connect with the games they will love and come back to. In the Moments tab, every post is a doorway to play. Players can click the Join button beneath each gameplay clip to start playing immediately. That’s the road to discovering a great new game. Chat: Connect and Play Across Games Chat is where players go to recommend games to friends, coordinate a play session, even jump into a game together. This matters because people don’t come back just for a game, they come back to connect and play with friends. When a friend says, “Hey, you have to try this game,” we want joining that game to be as easy as possible. Today, the Chat tab will appear for all chat-eligible players. Soon, we’ll make it possible for the conversation to continue within and across games so friends can stay seamlessly connected as they play without switching apps or coordinating on different devices. Built atop foundational features like age-checks to chat and Roblox Kids and Select accounts , Chat is available only when it's age-appropriate for players. With Trusted Friends and real-time chat rephrasing , we’re making it easier for players of all ages to connect—with the protections that help keep them safe. Me: Self-Expression, All in One Tab The Avatar tab is now the Me tab, making it simple to update a player’s profile information and their avatar’s look all in one place. Here, players can choose from several new avatar backgrounds, giving them one more way to express themselves. Build: Expanding What’s Possible on Roblox The public alpha of the Build tab, our new in-app creation feature , starts rolling out today to age-verified users 9 and older in New Zealand. Build is a mobile-first game-creation experience designed to work alongside Studio and share the same back end, models, and chat history. Starting today, public alpha creators can start a game on their phone in Build, then finesse it with the broader capabilities of Studio. Once the tab is fully launched, they’ll also be able to start in Studio and check on progress on their mobile device. With Build, we’re expanding not only the kinds of games Roblox supports, but who can create them. This is the beginning of a new chapter for Roblox players, with one home for connecting with friends, discovering what their friends and favorite video content creators are playing, expressing themselves, and maybe even building something entirely new. We can’t wait to see what the community does with it. * Availability and features will vary by age and region.

title: How to Use AI in Marketing: A Guide for Small Business Owners
summary: Learn how to use AI in marketing to get found, win leads, and drive repeat business. A practical, step-by-step guide for small business owners.
body_text: A homeowner fills out your contact form on Saturday night after their water heater fails. By the time you see the message Monday morning, they’ve already hired someone else. That kind of missed opportunity happens every day. Leads sit unanswered, review requests get forgotten, social media goes quiet, and your business becomes harder to find online. It’s rarely because you don’t care. Your day fills up quickly, and marketing often gets pushed aside. Learning how to use AI in marketing starts with solving these problems. AI can respond to inquiries, request reviews, create AI-generated social posts, and follow up with customers so you have more time to serve them. You don’t need to learn a dozen new tools or become a marketing expert. Start with one task that’s slowing your business down, prove it works, and build from there. In this guide, you’ll learn practical ways to use AI in your marketing, what tasks to automate first, and how Thryv® helps small businesses attract more customers, win more jobs, and drive repeat business with less manual work. Key Takeaways AI helps small businesses get found online, respond to leads faster, and bring customers back. Start by automating the task that’s costing you the most customers, such as review requests or lead follow-up. Fast responses and consistent follow-up help you win more jobs before customers choose another business. AI delivers the most value when your listings, reviews, website, and customer communication work together. What “Using AI in Marketing” Actually Means for a Small Business For a small business, using AI in marketing means letting software handle the repetitive work that often gets pushed to the bottom of your to-do list. That could be drafting a social media post, writing a blog post, sending a review request, following up with a new lead, or organizing customer information so you know who to contact next. Those tasks still get done while you’re focused on serving customers. Imagine you finish a water heater installation and head straight to your next appointment. Instead of needing to remember to request a review that evening, AI can send a personalized message while the experience is still fresh. A few more reviews each month can improve your visibility in local search results, strengthen your SEO (search engine optimization) efforts, and give future customers more confidence to call. Some AI tools use generative AI for content creation, while others automate follow-ups, reminders, and customer communication after you’ve set them up. More than 80% of small businesses already use artificial intelligence in marketing. The biggest opportunity comes from connecting those tools so you spend less time switching between apps while maintaining brand control. Keeping everything in one place makes day-to-day marketing much easier. For example, after you complete a plumbing repair, Thryv’s AI Content Assistant uses generative AI to turn your job details into a ready-to-publish social post, CaptionAI formats the caption for each platform, and Automated Reviews sends a personalized review request automatically. You approve the messaging before it goes live, giving you confidence that every piece of content reflects your business. How to Use AI to Get Found Online (Listings, Local SEO, Reviews) Customers can’t hire your business if they can’t find it. One of the easiest ways to improve your visibility is by keeping your online listings and Google Business Profile accurate and active. Incorrect business hours, phone numbers, or addresses can cost you calls. AI-powered business listings management software helps keep your information accurate across major directories. Posting updates, adding photos, and answering customer questions keeps your business looking active. After completing a landscaping project or plumbing repair, Thryv’s AI Content Assistant can turn your job details into ready-to-publish social posts, so your online presence stays current without starting every post from scratch. Reviews also play a major role in whether customers choose your business. Imagine two plumbers showing up in local search. One has recent five-star reviews with thoughtful responses. The other hasn’t received a new review in months. Many homeowners will call the business that appears more active and trusted. If collecting reviews has been inconsistent, Thryv’s Automated Reviews can send review requests automatically after each completed job, while AI Review Response helps draft personalized replies you can review before publishing. That keeps your online reputation growing without adding another item to your to-do list. Your website deserves attention, too. Thryv’s AI Website Builder helps create service pages, location-specific content, and FAQs built faster and SEO/AEO-optimized content that helps your business get found in Google Search, ChatGPT, and voice search. The same approach works for blogs, emails, and social media if you’re learning how to use AI for content creation across your business. Download the Guide to AI for Small Business Want the deeper playbook? Our free guide walks through practical, owner-ready ways to put AI to work across your marketing. GET FREE GUIDE How to Use AI to Convert More Leads (Lead Generation, Follow-Ups) Every missed follow-up is a job someone else books. A customer who fills out your contact form during lunch or sends a Facebook message after work usually expects a quick response. If they don’t hear back, they’ll often contact the next business on their list. AI helps prevent those missed opportunities by capturing every inquiry, responding quickly, and keeping follow-up moving until a customer books. Instead of relying on memory or handwritten notes, every lead stays organized, and every opportunity has a better chance of becoming revenue. Using AI for Lead Capture Leads come from phone calls, website forms, live chat, social media, and Google Business Profile. When they’re scattered across different places, it’s easy to miss one. Once it’s set up, Thryv’s AI Lead Insights captures those inquiries in one place and uses lead scoring to help identify which ones need immediate attention. For example, someone requesting emergency drain service today should probably be prioritized over someone requesting a remodeling estimate next month. If you’re finding it difficult to keep track of new inquiries across multiple channels, resources about AI tools for business development can help you understand how AI supports lead management. Thryv’s AI Lead Insights automatically captures missed calls, website forms, chats, and messages in one place, then uses machine learning and lead scoring to identify the inquiries most likely to become booked jobs and recommends a clear next step for each one. Automating Follow-Up Many customers don’t book the first time they reach out. They get busy, compare estimates, or forget to call back. Once it’s set up, AI sends timely follow-up emails or texts on schedule, creating consistent email marketing and customer communication without adding another task to your day while keeping your marketing workflows moving even when your schedule is full. For example, someone who requests an estimate on Tuesday could receive a confirmation within minutes, a reminder a few days later if they haven’t scheduled, and a final check-in before the opportunity goes cold. You create the sequence once, and every follow-up happens automatically. AI Response to Inbound Leads Customers don’t always reach out during business hours. A homeowner with a broken water heater at 9 p.m. may send a message expecting an answer before deciding who to call the next morning. AI chat tools can answer common questions, collect job details, and let customers know when they’ll hear from your team. That quick response helps keep the conversation moving while giving customers confidence that someone has already received their request. With Thryv, a missed call on Friday afternoon, a website form submitted that evening, and a Facebook message sent Saturday morning all land in one place, and AI Lead Insights flags who still needs a response. By Monday morning, you know exactly where to start instead of piecing together conversations from different apps. How to Use AI to Drive Repeat Business Staying in touch after the job helps bring customers back. AI automates review requests, maintenance reminders, seasonal promotions, and check-ins so you stay top of mind without adding more work. Start by automatically requesting reviews while each completed job is still fresh in the customer’s mind. Thryv’s Automated Reviews sends personalized review requests on schedule, making it easier to collect feedback while customers are most likely to respond. AI keeps customer relationships going by reconnecting with people at the right time. For example, after a water heater replacement, the customer could receive a review request shortly after the job, a 30-day check-in a few weeks later, and a maintenance reminder the following year. You build the sequence once using Thryv’s AI Automation Assistant , and it continues running automatically. Those consistent touchpoints create better customer experiences, generate repeat work, and help keep your schedule full without relying on memory. The same approach can also strengthen your online reputation, especially when you use AI for customer reviews to request feedback and respond consistently after every completed job. AI Marketing Tools vs. an All-in-One Platform: How to Avoid Tool Sprawl It’s easy to start collecting AI tools. One handles social posts, another manages reviews, another sends emails, and another manages chat. When those tools aren’t connected, leads, customer information, and email marketing can quickly fall out of sync. Keeping customer information connected helps AI coordinate review requests, follow-up messages, appointment reminders, and email marketing based on each customer’s latest activity. If you already rely on a specialized tool that integrates well with the rest of your business, it may still make sense to keep it. As you compare different AI marketing tools for small business , think about how well they fit into the way you already attract, communicate with, and retain customers. A Step-by-Step Plan to Start Using AI in Your Marketing This Month Start by solving the problem that’s costing you the most customers. If leads wait too long for a response, automate follow-up. If reviews are inconsistent, automate review requests. Many effective AI strategies for small businesses begin with one high-impact improvement. Here’s a simple four-week plan you can start this month. Week 1: Automate Review Requests Set up AI to automatically request reviews while the experience is still fresh. More recent reviews can improve your visibility in local search and give potential customers more confidence to contact you. Week 2: Centralize Your Leads Bring calls, website forms, chat messages, and social inquiries into one place so every lead gets a response. Week 3: Turn On Automated Follow-Up Create a simple sequence for new inquiries, whether that’s a confirmation message, a reminder, or a follow-up after an estimate. Once it’s in place, every lead receives consistent communication, even during your busiest weeks. Week 4: Schedule Content and Review Your Results Use AI to create and schedule social posts, then review where inquiries came from, how many reviews you earned, and how quickly leads received a response. If you’re using several AI tools, it may be time to simplify. Thryv’s AI-powered tools bring your visibility, customer communication, lead management, reviews, and follow-up together while helping protect customer data and data privacy. You can try core tools like Social Media Management, Reputation Management, Listings Management, and the AI-Powered Website Builder with a free trial so you spend less time managing software and more time helping customers. Where to Go From Here With AI in Your Marketing Growth often slows because simple marketing tasks don’t happen consistently. Leads wait for a response, reviews don’t get requested, and past customers drift away. You don’t have to automate everything to see results. Start with the task that’s costing you the most customers today. Once that process runs consistently, add the next one. Those small improvements help you get found online, respond faster, earn more repeat business, and spend less time on routine marketing. As you evaluate AI tools for your business, look for software that brings your visibility, reviews, follow-up, and customer communication together. That’s the approach behind Thryv’s AI-powered marketing tools. AI Content Assistant, AI Lead Insights, AI Automation Assistant, Automated Reviews, and AI Review Response help you spend less time managing marketing while turning more opportunities into booked jobs. FAQs About Using AI in Marketing A: The easiest place to start is with repetitive tasks that happen every day. AI systems can automate review requests, lead follow-up emails and texts, social media posts, content generation, appointment reminders, and responses to common customer questions. Those tasks save time while helping you stay responsive and support your digital marketing efforts. The biggest return often comes from responding to inquiries faster, earning more customer reviews, and bringing previous customers back for additional work. If you’re managing listings, reviews, customer communication, lead follow-up, social media, email marketing, content marketing, and campaign workflows, a unified platform can reduce duplicate work by keeping your customer information and marketing activities connected. title: Is a home equity loan a good idea?
summary: A home equity loan is a good idea only if you have a structured repayment plan and use the funds to increase your net worth or save on interest.
body_text: A home equity loan tends to make sense when the funds are used to strengthen your financial position or add lasting value. Financing home improvements Home renovations are among the most common and most justified uses of home equity. Projects that increase your property's value, like kitchen remodels or structural repairs, can deliver a meaningful return. As a bonus, interest may be tax-deductible if you use the funds to buy, build, or substantially improve your home. Check with a qualified tax professional before assuming your interest qualifies. Consolidating high-interest debt Replacing high-interest credit card balances with a single, lower fixed-rate home equity loan can reduce what you pay in interest and simplify your monthly obligations. The trade-off: you're converting unsecured debt into debt backed by your home, so consistent repayment is essential. Covering emergency or major expenses When urgent costs arise like medical bills, critical home repairs, a home equity loan can provide stability at a lower rate than most other borrowing options. It's best used as a last resort, with a clear plan to repay. Enjoying fixed rates and predictable payments Unlike a home equity line of credit (HELOC), a home equity loan typically carries a fixed rate and term. Your monthly payments stay consistent, making it easier to plan and budget over the life of the loan. A home equity loan can become a financial burden when used for the wrong reasons or under the wrong conditions. Discretionary or luxury spending Using your home as collateral for vacations, weddings, or other non-essential expenses puts long-term equity at risk for short-term wants. Your home's equity represents years of built-up value — spending it on depreciating experiences rarely pays off. Financial instability or high debt load If your income is unpredictable or you're already managing significant debt, adding another monthly payment could strain your budget and put your home at risk. A stable income, manageable debt-to-income (DTI) ratio, and existing emergency savings are the baseline before taking on a home equity loan. Falling home values If property values decline after you borrow, you could end up owing more than your home is worth — a situation known as negative equity. This can limit your ability to sell or refinance until values recover. No clear repayment plan Borrowing without a defined strategy can backfire. Using home equity to replace one debt with another isn't progress unless the new terms meaningfully improve your position. Know exactly how you'll use and repay the funds before signing. Your home is collateral Because the loan is secured by your home, missed payments can lead to foreclosure — a legal process in which the lender takes ownership of your property. Only borrow what you're confident you can repay. Fees and closing costs Expect costs like appraisal fees, closing costs, and possibly prepayment penalties. Factor these into your total borrowing expense when comparing options. Temporary credit score impact Taking on a large loan can temporarily lower your credit score by increasing your overall debt load. This typically recovers over time with consistent on-time payments. Axos home equity loans Put your home's equity to work. A home equity loan from Axos lets you borrow against the value you've built; with a fixed rate, predictable payments, and no surprises. Ideal for major renovations where you need a lump sum upfront. Apply Now Learn More A home equity loan isn't the only way to access funds. Depending on your situation, one of these may be a better fit: HELOC: Offers flexibility for ongoing or phased expenses, with a variable rate and the ability to draw funds as needed to a set limit. Personal loan: Unsecured and faster to qualify for in some cases, though it typically carries a higher interest rate. Cash-out refinance: Replaces your existing mortgage with a new, larger one — giving you a lump sum upfront but resetting your loan term. Home improvement loans or grants: Designed specifically for renovations and sometimes available through state or local programs. Is a home equity loan a good idea? For homeowners with stable income, solid credit, and a clear plan, it can be one of the most cost-effective ways to fund major expenses or reduce high-interest debt. For those in uncertain financial positions or without a defined repayment strategy, the risks outweigh the benefits. Take time to compare lenders, review your full financial picture, and consider speaking with a financial advisor before making a decision. Ready to explore your options? Learn more about home equity loans from Axos and find out how much you may be able to borrow. Frequently asked questions How much can I borrow with a home equity loan? Most lenders allow you to borrow up to 80–85% of your home's appraised value, minus what you still owe on your mortgage. The exact amount depends on your equity, credit profile, and the lender's requirements. What's the difference between a home equity loan and a HELOC? A home equity loan gives you a lump sum at a fixed rate — predictable and straightforward. A HELOC works more like a credit card: you draw funds as needed up to a limit, usually at a variable rate. Home equity loans suit defined, one-time expenses; HELOCs work better for ongoing costs. Is a HELOC better than a home equity loan? It depends on how you plan to use the funds. For a single large expense with a known cost, a home equity loan's fixed rate offers more stability. For projects with uncertain or phased costs, a HELOC's flexibility may be more practical. What can I use a home equity loan for? Common uses include home renovations, debt consolidation, medical expenses, and education costs. The strongest use cases are those that add long-term value or reduce what you're paying in interest elsewhere.

This crisis is fueled by a broken healthcare system that has historically deprioritized women’s health during one of the most critical moments in their lives. The need for deeper, more attentive care is paramount, and doulas can bridge the gap. Doulas are non-medical professionals who provide vital education, advocacy, and emotional support for people who are pregnant, giving birth, and recovering from labor. Research shows that engaging a qualified doula during or after pregnancy can: Improve live-birth rates Reduce the frequency of expensive C-sections Lower rates of postpartum depression and anxiety Decrease complications in labor and delivery Shorten recovery time from labor, getting parents back to work sooner But not all doulas are created equal, and there isn't a standardized vetting process to ensure quality care from one professional to another. This quality gap can create risks to the health and safety of women, babies, and families. Carrot has always recognized the valuable role these caregivers play, by helping our members afford and access their services. Carrot is proud to announce our new doula network : a global, in-network program of highly qualified caregivers — rigorously vetted by Carrot — to ensure the highest quality experience for every member. Members can now more easily access the best professionals possible for prenatal and postnatal care, because all doulas within Carrot's network complete a rigorous vetting process. title: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern Respond to STB’s Request for Supplemental Information, Submitting First Round of Their Responses
summary: Union Pacific Corporation (NYSE: UNP) and Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE: NSC) today submitted the first portion of their responses to the Surface Transportation Board’s (STB) May 28, 2026, request for additional information to support their accepted merger application.
body_text: Union Pacific Corporation (NYSE: UNP) and Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE: NSC) today submitted the first portion of their responses to the Surface Transportation Board’s (STB) May 28, 2026, request for additional information to support their accepted merger application. Today’s filing addresses the STB’s questions regarding Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis (TRRA), Kansas City Terminal Railway (KCT) and TTX Company. These entities are jointly owned with other Class I railroads, operated by independent management teams and governed by non-discrimination policies. Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern do not control these companies today and remain firm in their commitment that they will not control them post-merger. The merger application and today’s supplemental filing provide the STB with options to implement this commitment, up to and including divestiture. In particular, for the TRRA, the filing provides clear evidence that the other Class I railroads who are vocally opposing the merger are using the TRRA as a pawn in their efforts to stop or delay the merger. This includes failing to appear at a properly convened special meeting for the sole purpose of discussing ways to reduce Union Pacific’s ownership in TRRA post-merger. Only Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern board members attended the meeting called by TRRA’s corporate secretary, while members from BNSF, CSX and Canadian National did not show. Connecting Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern’s end-to-end networks will finally give American shippers single-line transcontinental rail service, creating a stronger alternative to long-haul trucking, making the entire supply chain more competitive, and putting downward pressure on truck and rail prices. The opportunities opened by the merger for shifting freight from truck to rail are projected to save shippers an estimated $3.5 billion annually. Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern have consistently welcomed rigorous regulatory review of the proposed merger, and today’s submission reflects that commitment. The responses to the STB’s other requests for additional information will follow by July 27, 2026. The STB accepted as complete the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger application on May 28, a positive step toward creating America’s first transcontinental railroad. The railroads are committed to working constructively with the STB toward a mid-2027 completion. For more information, visit AmericasGreatConnection.com . ##### About Union Pacific Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) delivers the goods families and businesses use every day with safe, reliable, and efficient service. Operating in 23 western states, the company connects its customers and communities to the global economy. Trains are the most environmentally responsible way to move freight, helping Union Pacific protect future generations. More information about Union Pacific is available at www.up.com . About Norfolk Southern Since 1827, Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE: NSC) and its predecessor companies have safely moved the goods and materials that drive the U.S. economy. Today, it operates a 22-state freight transportation network. Committed to furthering sustainability, Norfolk Southern helps its customers avoid approximately 15 million tons of yearly carbon emissions by shipping via rail. Its dedicated team members deliver approximately 7 million carloads annually, from agriculture to consumer goods. Norfolk Southern also has the most extensive intermodal network in the eastern U.S. It serves a majority of the country's population and manufacturing base, with connections to every major container port on the Atlantic coast as well as major ports across the Gulf Coast and Great Lakes. title: We Break Down the Best AI Voice Agents for Appointment Booking

body_text: 7 Reasons You Should Use AI Voice Agents for Appointment Booking Before we dive into the good stuff, it’s probably helpful to set the scene a little bit, so we wanted to give you a quick overview of how exactly AI voice agents can help you improve your conversion rates and fill your calendar. Handle every inbound call without gaps We’ve seen how easy it is for calls to slip through during busy hours or after closing time. An AI voice agent picks up instantly, every time, meaning it keeps your calendar moving even when your team is offline. Reduce manual scheduling work Booking appointments manually adds up fast. Between checking availability, confirming details, and updating systems, it eats into time that could be spent elsewhere. With an AI voice agent, those steps happen automatically. We’ve tested setups where bookings go straight into the calendar and CRM without anyone touching it. And we built telli to do just that. Keep responses consistent Different team members handle calls differently. Some are great at guiding conversations, others miss key steps. AI voice agents follow the same flow every time and most platforms allow you to define exactly what that flow is. From collecting names to confirming time slots, the process stays clean and predictable. Speed up booking time When someone calls, they usually want to lock in a time quickly and AI voice agents are good at moving through the process fast. We’ve noticed shorter call times and higher booking completion rates when the process is streamlined. Capture and qualify leads automatically Not every caller is ready to book. Some need to be filtered or routed. AI voice agents can ask basic questions, tag the lead, and either book the appointment or pass it to the right person. This ensures that no lead slips through the cracks. Lower operational costs Hiring and training staff to handle calls full-time can get expensive. AI voice agents handle a large volume of calls at a fraction of that cost. From what we’ve seen, even a simple setup can replace hours of repetitive work each week. Scale without adding headcount As call volume grows, so does the pressure on your team. AI voice agents scale instantly. Whether it’s 10 calls or 1,000, the experience stays the same. We’ve seen this make a big difference for businesses running campaigns or seasonal promotions, when call volume naturally spikes but companies don’t necessarily want to add headcount for temporary increases. How AI Appointment Booking Works AI appointment booking can be as simple or as complex as you make it. It just depends on the solution you chose, whether that’s a more developer-focused voice AI platform like Vapi or something more out-of-the-box, like telli . In this section, we’ll focus on what the process looks like if you choose telli. Step 1: Create the agent When you set up an AI voice agent in telli, you can either pick a template or upload your own script depending on how custom you want the flow to be. For most appointment-setting use cases, we’ve found templates get you live faster, then you tweak from there. You define the goal early on. That could be booking consultations, scheduling demos, or handling inbound appointment requests. Once that’s clear, the platform generates a base structure for the agent. Step 2: Shape how the agent sounds This part matters more than most people expect. In telli, you can adjust the agent’s name, voice, language, and speaking speed. We’ve run tests on a few variations, and even small tweaks like slowing the voice slightly or adding light background noise can make calls feel more natural. You also set the opening message for inbound and outbound calls. This is where the agent introduces itself and sets expectations for the call. Step 3: Add customer context Before the agent starts making or receiving calls, it needs context. In telli, this comes from your contact data. You can pass in details like name, company, past interactions, or campaign source. We’ve used this to personalize calls in a simple way. For example, the agent can reference where the lead came from or what they showed interest in. That keeps the conversation grounded instead of generic. Step 4: Connect your calendar This is where appointment setting actually happens. telli connects directly to tools like Calendly, Cal.com, or HubSpot Meetings. You can also plug in a custom calendar setup if needed. During the call, the agent checks availability in real time, suggests time slots based on the caller’s preferences, and books the appointment once confirmed. The flow is straightforward. Ask for a time, suggest options, lock it in, then confirm the details. Step 5: Run test calls and refine Before going live, we always run test calls. telli makes this easy by letting you call a test contact and review recordings and transcripts right after. This is where you catch small issues. Maybe the agent talks too fast, misses a step, or handles edge cases poorly. You adjust the prompt, test again, and repeat until the flow feels smooth. Step 6: Automate follow-ups and CRM updates Once calls are running, telli pushes data back into your system. Every call can trigger updates in your CRM with transcripts, outcomes, and booking details. We’ve seen this save a lot of manual work. Instead of logging calls or updating contact records, everything syncs automatically. You can also track which calls led to booked appointments and which didn’t. Step 7: Keep improving the conversation flow After launch, the work doesn’t really stop. We usually review call data regularly and adjust the agent’s behavior based on what’s happening in real conversations. And you should too. That means updating prompts, adding better instructions for handling edge cases, and tightening the booking flow. Small changes here tend to improve booking rates over time. We designed it so our voice agents answer every call 24/7, understand why someone is calling, capture the right details, route calls when needed, and book appointments directly into your calendar. On the booking side, we’ve made it flexible. You can connect tools like Calendly, Cal.com, HubSpot Calendar, or even your own custom setup. During the call, the agent checks availability, suggests time slots, confirms the booking, and logs everything automatically. The biggest impact, though, is what happens after the appointment is booked. Every interaction, including transcripts, notes, appointment data, and outcomes, syncs back into systems like HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, Zoho, and Microsoft Dynamics. For teams handling a high volume of calls, this usually means fewer missed opportunities, less manual work, and a steady increase in booked appointments. {{usecases}} Retell Retell is a strong option for teams that want a flexible AI voice agent for scheduling calls, demos, or service appointments. Completed call volume increased fourfold, call minutes rose by 250 percent, and half of all inquiries are fully handled by AI. enerix did not change its support model because there was no need to. Most teams reach basic value fast. Recurring invoices and automated reminders take days, not months. The heavier lift is wiring up bank feeds and ERP systems for full cash application. That’s where the difficulty rating jumps from low to medium . Organizations with advanced AP automation report a 57% reduction in processing errors and processing up to 5 times faster than traditional methods. Top performers get costs as low as $2.18 per invoice** against an industry average of **$10.89 . And the AI gets smarter as you use it. When your team corrects a match by hand, the system learns and improves the next one. That compounding effect is what separates genuinely smart tools from rule-based automation that never adapts. Where AI Closes the Loop The angle that matters most: turning overdue payments into proactive, personalized outreach. Old systems flagged a late invoice and stopped there. Smart platforms escalate on their own, picking the channel and tone based on the customer’s payment history. Blixo pairs a matching engine for cash application with automated collections across email, SMS, phone, and mail, so a missed payment triggers the next best action instead of a manual to-do. Skip AI-heavy invoicing if you send a handful of invoices a month. The setup won’t pay back. For any team drowning in reconciliation or chasing overdue accounts, the math is clear: automate it. Why Smart Invoicing Matters Late payments break businesses. A single invoice takes over 20 days to process by hand, and nearly 20% of those invoices carry errors from manual data entry. When cash sits trapped in overdue receivables, you can’t pay suppliers, cover payroll, or fund growth. That’s the real cost of a broken invoicing loop. Smart invoicing closes the send-to-paid gap with AI. The best platforms in 2026 don’t stop at generating a clean invoice. They extract data, match incoming payments, flag exceptions, and trigger collections the moment a payment slips. This is where AI earns its keep, turning a passive document into an active driver of cash flow. What Problems Does Smart Invoicing Actually Solve? It kills the manual bottlenecks that delay payment: slow data entry, mismatched payments, and reactive collections. The impact shows up fastest in days sales outstanding, where automated dispute handling trims 15 to 20% off the time it takes to close an account and free up working capital. The bigger win is what happens after the invoice goes out. Cash application matching, once a spreadsheet nightmare, now runs on its own. When a payment lands, AI ties it to the right invoice with nobody touching anything, even across partial payments and consolidated remittances that used to stall a whole team. Fraud protection comes built in. AI flags forged, duplicated, or altered invoices in real time. Duplicate payments alone drain an estimated 0.1 to 0.5% of total spend at companies without automated controls, and anomaly detection catches those before a bad payment clears. Who Benefits Most From AI-Powered Invoicing? High-volume finance teams gain the most. 32% of enterprises process over 100,000 invoices a year, and manual handling at that scale burns money and staff hours. Automation redeploys that AP headcount toward analysis and vendor management instead of keying data. The savings scale with volume. Mid-sized firms handling 5,000 to 10,000 invoices monthly save an average of $250,000 a year** after moving to AI automation. Enterprises above 100,000 invoices annually report savings around **$2.1 million in direct processing costs. Real results back this up. One beverage bottler recovered $33.4 million with a 34-day resolution time, well ahead of the 90-day industry average. Not marginal gains. The difference between chasing cash and controlling it. Why Proactive Collections Change the Game The old model waited for payments to go overdue, then scrambled. AI flips that. It watches every invoice, spots slippage early, and launches personalized outreach automatically. No spreadsheet, no manual follow-up list. This is the loop the top platforms are built around. Early, tailored reminders lift on-time payment rates by as much as 20% , and dynamic scheduling times each nudge to the moment an account is most likely to pay. Those recovered hours go toward strategy, not data entry. That’s the shift worth paying for: collections that reach out before a customer forgets, in language tuned to that account. You stop reacting to overdue payments and start preventing them. Core Technologies Driving Smart Invoicing Four technologies power every smart invoicing system: optical character recognition (OCR) , machine learning , natural language processing (NLP) , and robotic process automation (RPA) . Together they read an invoice, understand it, match it to a payment, and fire the next action without human data entry. This stack is what separates real 2026 platforms from basic billing tools. The payoff shows up at the collections end. When these technologies extract clean data and match payments accurately, the system knows exactly which invoices are overdue and can push personalized outreach the moment cash slips. How Do OCR and Computer Vision Read an Invoice? OCR converts paper, image, or PDF invoices into machine-readable text. Computer vision goes further, capturing both the visual layout and the meaning of fields on the page. OCR handles the first mile, turning static documents into structured fields. But raw OCR has limits. Accuracy runs 79-88% on clean scans and drops to 28-62% on blurred or skewed images . Even at high accuracy, one wrong character in an invoice number or bank detail can trigger costly rework. That’s why modern platforms pair OCR with vision-aware models. The LayoutLM transformer captures semantic and visual cues together, beating older approaches on messy layouts. This matters most for infrequent, long-tail suppliers whose invoices never look the same twice. What Does Machine Learning Add to Invoice Processing? Machine learning lets the system learn from historical data and adapt to new invoice formats over time. It reads past invoices to sharpen extraction accuracy and drive automatic matching between purchase orders and payments. The gains are concrete. Models trained on a company’s own vendor history keep improving with every document, so a format that failed last quarter clears cleanly today. AI-driven systems cut manual entry errors by 93.2% in banking deployments, and ML classifiers can route invoices to the correct GL code with over 90% precision once trained. Matching is where ML closes the loop. High match rates mean the platform reconciles incoming payments instantly, so your team sees which accounts are genuinely overdue instead of chasing ghosts caused by unapplied cash. How Do NLP and Automation Complete the Loop? NLP interprets the unstructured text on an invoice, pulling meaning from free-form fields that fixed templates miss. RPA then runs the downstream steps: validation, approval routing, and follow-up. NLP combined with OCR lets platforms read invoices in multiple languages and formats without custom rules for each vendor. That flexibility feeds straight into collections. When the system understands context, it can categorize an overdue account and match the tone and timing of outreach to that specific customer. Automation ties it together. Systems cut processing from 15 minutes to under 3 minutes per invoice and run with minimal supervision. Anomaly-detection models flag forged or duplicated invoices in real time, protecting cash before it leaks. The end state is proactive. Instead of a human noticing a late payment weeks later, the platform catches the slip the day it happens and launches follow-up automatically. That’s the line between passive billing and an active cash-collection engine. Talent Retention and AI in Accounts Payable AI doesn’t replace your accounts payable team. It strips out the tedious work that drives people to quit. When the platform handles data capture, matching, and collections outreach, your AP staff stop keying numbers into spreadsheets and start managing exceptions and vendor relationships. That shift matters for retention. Manual invoice work is repetitive and draining. Every keying error triggers rework that frustrates skilled staff and eats hours they’d rather spend elsewhere. Automation frees those people for analysis, dispute resolution, and the personalized collections follow-up that actually recovers cash. How Does AI Improve Talent Retention in Accounts Payable? AI keeps AP talent by cutting the grind and lifting the role. When a system processes invoices up to 5 times faster and pushes accuracy to 97-98% , your team spends its hours on judgment work instead of data entry. That turns a cost-center job into a strategic one. Take the collections side. Instead of chasing overdue invoices one email at a time, your staff supervise AI that flags slipping payments and drafts personalized outreach automatically. They step in only for the tricky accounts. More engaging work, and engaged people stay. The payoff shows up in the numbers. Finance teams that shift staff off manual entry report far lower turnover in AP roles, and roughly 80% of employees say automation gives them more time for work they find meaningful. Motivated teams focused on cash recovery beat those buried in keystrokes. What Are the Challenges of Adopting AI in AP? The biggest hurdle isn’t technology. It’s change management. Staff worry AI will take their jobs, so adoption stalls unless you show them it’s an assistant, not a replacement. Integration is next. Your AI solution has to connect cleanly with existing ERP and accounting systems. Pick a platform that integrates without heavy customization and scales as your invoice volume grows. Accuracy on messy inputs trips up a lot of rollouts. OCR reads clean scans well but drops sharply on blurred or skewed images. A human-in-the-loop review catches those flagged entries and keeps quality high while capturing your team’s institutional knowledge. Best Practices for AI Adoption in AP Start by mapping your current workflows. Find the pain points before you buy anything, so you know what the AI actually needs to fix. Involve your AP team early. The Rillion team put it simply: “AI systems are designed to learn and adapt, so take advantage of this by retraining and updating your AI model periodically.” - Rillion Team A practical checklist for rolling out AI in accounts payable: Audit workflows first to pinpoint where errors and delays cluster. Choose a platform that fits your ERP without custom rebuilds. Involve AP staff in setup to drive adoption and gather feedback. Build in human review for flagged and complex invoices. Retrain the model regularly as new invoice formats appear. Reframe roles toward collections strategy and vendor management. Training seals it. Teach your team to supervise the AI, read its analytics, and own the personalized collections outreach that closes the loop. That’s where retained talent earns its keep, and where overdue payments turn into recovered cash. Future Trends in AI Invoice Processing The next wave of invoice AI won’t stop at reading documents faster. It’s moving toward predicting when a customer will pay, matching cash the moment it lands, and reaching out before an invoice goes overdue. That’s where the 2026 platforms are already heading. The shift is from reactive to proactive. Instead of chasing payments after they’re late, AI models forecast payment behavior and trigger personalized collections the second cash flow signals a problem. This closes the send-to-paid loop that older billing tools left wide open. What Emerging Technologies Are Changing Invoice AI? Transformer-based extraction is the biggest near-term change. Models like LayoutLM read invoice layout, text, and visual cues together, so they handle formats they’ve never seen before. This matters most for long-tail suppliers who bill infrequently and in wildly different formats. Traditional OCR struggles here, especially on low-resolution scans. Transformer models close the gap between familiar and unfamiliar layouts, which means fewer exceptions land on a human’s desk. Fraud detection is the other fast-moving frontier. AI flags forged, duplicated, or altered documents. For collections, that protection matters. You don’t want to chase a payment against an invoice that was manipulated in the first place. How Will AI Reshape Accounts Payable and Cash Application? AI is turning accounts payable into a predictive function, not a processing one. The real leap is payment-timing prediction: models trained on a customer’s past behavior can estimate a pay date within a few days of actual settlement. That forecast lets finance teams plan working capital instead of guessing at it. Cash application is catching up fast. Remittance-matching engines can now reconcile split payments, short pays, and lump-sum deposits across multiple invoices automatically. When cash matches itself at that level, the system knows instantly which accounts are current and which need outreach. That’s where collections intelligence comes in. Once payments match themselves, the platform ranks overdue accounts by risk and generates outreach tuned to each customer’s history. A reliable payer who’s a few days late gets a gentle nudge. A chronic delayer gets firmer, earlier contact. Real-time payment rails push this further. Instant settlement networks mean a matched payment updates the ledger in seconds, so you see receivable gaps as they open rather than at month-end. Faster visibility, faster action. What Challenges Still Hold AI Invoice Processing Back? AI still needs a human safety net. Confidence scoring helps: models route low-confidence extractions to a reviewer while auto-processing the clean ones, so people spend time only where judgment adds value. Skip that layer and you risk sending collections outreach based on bad data. Two practical limits stand out. First, paper and PDF invoices still dominate many supplier bases, so capture quality stays a real constraint on downstream matching. Second, AI models drift as invoice formats change. You have to retrain them periodically to keep extraction and matching sharp. The honest read: AI won’t fully automate collections judgment yet. It handles capture, matching, and routine follow-up brilliantly. Disputes, negotiations, and relationship calls still belong to your team. The future isn’t a robot chasing payments. It’s AI clearing the busywork so your people run smarter, earlier, more personalized outreach. Feature Checklist for Selecting an AI Invoicing Platform Picking the right platform comes down to one question: does it close the send-to-paid loop, or just print pretty invoices? The best 2026 platforms automate the full cycle, from data capture through cash application and collections outreach. Use this checklist to separate real automation from surface-level billing tools. Score each platform on the categories below. A tool can nail data extraction and still fail you if it can’t match payments or trigger follow-up when cash slips. Judge the whole loop, not one piece. What Core Features Should an AI Invoicing Platform Have? The core four: automated data extraction, cash application matching, exception handling, and collections intelligence that acts the moment a payment goes overdue. Start with extraction accuracy, but test it against your own documents, not the vendor’s demo set. Ask how the platform handles line-item detail, not just header fields. Multi-line invoices with mixed tax rates and partial quantities are where a lot of tools quietly break. Run a batch of your messiest real-world scans through a trial before you sign anything. Then check what happens after extraction. Look for: Cash application matching that pairs incoming payments to open invoices automatically Exception handling that flags mismatches for human review instead of silently guessing Collections intelligence that sends personalized outreach when an invoice ages past due Multi-format capture across email, PDF, and scanned sources Confidence scoring on each extracted field so your team knows what to double-check Fraud detection that flags in real time The collections piece is where most tools fall short. Extraction and matching are table stakes now. A platform that knows an invoice is late and does nothing is only half a solution. How Do You Evaluate Security and Compliance? The platform has to protect financial data, meet regulatory requirements, and keep a human in the loop for high-risk decisions. One financial services firm cut compliance risk simply by automating and standardizing its invoice workflow. Ask where your data lives and how it moves. Look for encryption at rest and in transit, SOC 2 Type II certification, and role-based access controls that limit who can approve or edit payment records. Vendors that dodge these questions are telling you something. Run through this compliance checklist: Human-in-the-loop review for flagged or low-confidence entries Audit trails on every extraction, match, and payment action Multi-language support if you invoice globally across regions Fraud and anomaly detection to catch forged or photoshopped invoices before they clear And retrain your model periodically. AI systems learn and adapt, so a model tuned to your invoice mix stays accurate as formats and suppliers change. Does It Integrate and Scale With Your Business? The platform should connect to your existing ERP and accounting systems and handle volume growth without adding headcount. AI-enhanced ERP integrations report 65% faster processing than standard AP workflows. Volume is the real test. Ask how the platform behaves during month-end and quarter-close spikes, when invoice traffic can jump 3-5x over a normal day. A tool that runs fine on a quiet Tuesday but queues for hours under load costs you the savings it promised. Ask vendors for peak-throughput numbers, not just averages. Before you commit, map your current workflow and find the pain points. Involve your AP team in the choice. Their buy-in decides whether the tool gets used or ignored. Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can small businesses with low invoice volume benefit from AI invoicing? Businesses sending fewer than a handful of invoices monthly gain little from AI-heavy platforms, since setup effort won’t pay back. However, smaller firms using recurring billing or facing frequent overdue accounts may still benefit from automated reminders, which deploy in days with low integration difficulty. 2. How does AI invoicing handle invoices in multiple languages? NLP combined with OCR lets platforms read invoices across multiple languages and formats without custom rules per vendor. This flexibility supports global invoicing and feeds collections intelligence, letting the system categorize overdue accounts and tune outreach tone to each customer’s context regardless of the original document language. 3. What happens when AI cannot confidently read an invoice? Confidence scoring routes low-confidence extractions to a human reviewer while auto-processing clean documents. This human-in-the-loop layer catches blurred or skewed scans where OCR accuracy drops. Reviewers correct flagged entries, capturing institutional knowledge and preventing collections outreach based on inaccurate data. 4. How do AI invoicing platforms perform during month-end volume spikes? Invoice traffic can jump 3-5x above normal during month-end and quarter-close periods. Evaluate platforms on peak-throughput numbers rather than averages, since tools that run smoothly on quiet days may queue for hours under load, erasing the cost savings the automation promised. 5. What security certifications should an AI invoicing platform have? Look for SOC 2 Type II certification, encryption at rest and in transit, and role-based access controls limiting who can approve or edit payment records. Audit trails on every extraction, match, and payment action are essential. Vendors that avoid these questions signal weaker data protection standards. 6. Does AI replace accounts payable staff? AI removes tedious data entry rather than replacing AP teams. Staff shift toward exception handling, dispute resolution, vendor management, and personalized collections. Roughly 80% of employees say automation gives them more time for meaningful work, and finance teams report lower AP turnover after moving off manual keying. 7. How accurately can AI predict when a customer will pay? Payment-timing prediction models trained on a customer’s past behavior can estimate settlement dates within a few days of actual payment. This forecast helps finance teams plan working capital and lets platforms rank overdue accounts by risk, sending reliable payers gentle nudges and chronic delayers firmer, earlier contact.

body_text: Cheniere Partners Declares Quarterly Distributions Download as PDF July 28, 2026 8:30am EDT HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. (“Cheniere Partners”) (NYSE: CQP) today declared (i) a cash distribution of $0.820 per common unit to unitholders of record as of August 7, 2026, comprised of a base amount equal to $0.775 and a variable amount equal to $0.045, and (ii) the related distribution to its general partner. These distributions are payable on August 14, 2026. Publicly traded partnerships that earn net income in a calendar year that is effectively connected with the conduct of a US trade or business are generally required to withhold US income tax from distributions paid to foreign persons. The portion of our quarterly cash distributions that are paid to foreign persons will generally be subject to US withholding tax. This press release serves as qualified notice to nominees as provided for under Treasury Regulation Section 1.1446-4 and 1.446(f)-4. Please note that 100 percent of Cheniere Partners’ distributions to foreign investors are attributable to income that is effectively connected with a US trade or business and subject to withholding under Treasury Regulation Sections 1.1446-1 – 1.1446-6. Accordingly, all of Cheniere Partners’ distributions to foreign investors are subject to federal income tax withholding at the highest applicable effective tax rate. Furthermore, 100 percent of Cheniere Partners’ distributions to foreign investors is in excess of cumulative net income for purposes of Treasury Regulation Section 1.1446(f)-4(c)(2)(iii). Nominees are treated as withholding agents responsible for withholding distributions received by them on behalf of foreign investors. The 2026 Tesla Model Y Dual-Track Strategy: Deciding Between Standard Value and Premium Luxuries for US and European Families
